prompt: A ketone with molecular formula C₆H₁₂O (M⁺ = 100) shows a strong fragment at m/z = 58. What rearrangement explains this loss of 42?

options.label: McLafferty rearrangement (loses propene, gives enol fragment m/z=58)
α-cleavage (would give an acylium ion at ~43 or so)

explanation: McLafferty: carbonyl with γ-H → 6-membered TS, transfers γ-H to O, cleaves α-β bond, loses an alkene. For 2-hexanone (M=100), losing propene (42) gives an enol cation at m/z=58. Classic diagnostic for carbonyl compounds with γ-hydrogens.
